candidate_relations.reason: Aggressive melanoma is a behavior descriptor missing stage IIA, subsequent metastasis, and the second primary.
Nodular melanoma is an incompatible growth-pattern subtype not specified by the reference composite.
A compound/dysplastic nevus describes the involuting pigmented lesion, not the melanomas.
Cutaneous melanoma is the parent disease missing stage, later metastasis, and second primary.
Lymphoma is a different malignancy.
Spitz nevus is a benign/spitzoid melanocytic tumor, not this invasive melanoma course.
Superficial spreading melanoma asserts a histologic growth pattern not required and incomplete versus the composite.
Advanced melanoma captures later progression but omits initial IIA staging and the second primary.
High-risk melanoma is a prognostic label, not the full composite.
Metastatic melanoma names later nodal/skin metastasis but omits initial IIA disease and the second primary.
BRAF V600E mutant melanoma matches only the first tumor; the second primary was BRAF V600E negative.
Invasive melanoma is true of the index lesion (Breslow 2.6 mm) but incomplete versus the composite.
Merkel cell carcinoma is a different cutaneous malignancy.
Desmoplastic melanoma is an incompatible histologic subtype.
Locoregional recurrence of melanoma is one later event, not the full reference.
Primary mucosal melanoma conflicts with cutaneous cervical/skin disease.
Intermediate-thickness melanoma (2.6 mm) describes the index T-category without later metastasis or second primary.
BRAF V600E mutation-associated melanoma again omits the BRAF-negative second primary and staging composite.
Histology of a compound nevus with melanophages refers to the involuting lesion, not melanoma.
Acral lentiginous melanoma asserts an incompatible anatomic subtype.

case_quality_flags: Composite requires initial stage IIA melanoma, later metastasis, and a BRAF-discordant second primary; no candidate contains all three.
